- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows (especially 1-3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or flat — model tends to push upward too aggressively.
- Underestimate late-period spikes (especially 25-30 days ahead) when true price surges occur after a calm or downward trend — model misses momentum buildup.
- When sentiment is consistently 0.00 (no signal), model should not assume bullish bias — avoid upward drift unless recent price action shows clear momentum.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if forecast shows a sharp peak followed by a drop, model often overshoots the peak and fails to correct downward quickly.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates the final price — especially if recent 10-15 day prices are rising — apply downward adjustment of 1-3% for final days.
- If sentiment history is all 0.00, model should not rely on historical volatility — instead, use recent price mean or 14-day moving average as anchor.
